title: China Club sign and invitation
lede: April Greiman’s identity for the China Club restaurant in Los Angeles: a round neon sign with spaced, doubled letters, and a tilted opening invitation with rules, triangles, and a squiggle.
summary: Round black neon sign with spaced “C H I N A  C L U B” in white and blue and a red squiggle; a black-and-red tilted invitation. April Greiman, 1980.

source.label: People’s Graphic Design Archive: Signage for China Club

made: 1980 (invitation dated by the People’s Graphic Design Archive; the sign is undated there)

evidence.note: Inspected two People’s Graphic Design Archive images: a night photograph of the sign (1118 × 1098) and a photograph of the opened invitation ([item 1819](https://peoplesgdarchive.org/item/1819/china-club-invitation), 970 × 1452). Not stored. The owners of the physical objects are not stated.

styles.note: Clear example of the style in three dimensions: spaced letters, a doubled offset layer, bars, and loose geometric marks, carried into neon and a die-cut card.

context: The People’s Graphic Design Archive credits the sign and the invitation to April Greiman for the China Club, California, and dates the invitation 1980. [Sign](https://peoplesgdarchive.org/item/4146/signage-for-china-club), [invitation](https://peoplesgdarchive.org/item/1819/china-club-invitation).
The invitation lists April Greiman and Jayme Odgers among the credits and gives the address 8338 W Third Street, Los Angeles.
observed: The sign is a black disc on a pale wall, with two dark bars behind it at an angle.
“CHINA” and “CLUB” are white neon capitals with wide spaces between the letters, set on a rising diagonal. A blue copy of each letter sits slightly offset behind it.
A red and yellow neon squiggle rises from the top left edge of the disc.
The invitation is a folded card with a trapezoid outline, black above and red below.
On the invitation, event details sit on thin parallel rules that tilt; the year is set as “1  9  8  0” with wide spaces. The credits on the red half run upside down along diagonal rules.
White triangles, round punched holes, a thin wavy line, and short rules are scattered over both halves.
interpretation: The offset blue copy in the neon is the sign-maker’s version of an overprint: two film layers that do not quite register. The invitation uses tilted rules as a staff for spaced type, as in Weingart’s covers.
borrow: Set a short name in spaced capitals on a diagonal, with an offset second colour behind it.
Put event details on tilted hairline rules instead of a straight list.
Use one free squiggle as a counterpoint to straight bars.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The design belongs to April Greiman or her client; the photographs’ owners are not stated.
